To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the QOL of breast cancer patients is significantly impaired during the first 15 months after the diagnosis, that the impairment is more pronounced in patients with metastatic disease, and that psychosocial factors, in particular social support and the presence of depressive symptoms, are important predictors of QOL in this patient population.
the quality of life and the psychosocial adjustment of older women with breast cancer were similar to those of women of a similar age without breast cancer.
the majority of older women who are diagnosed with breast cancer have a good quality of life and a high level of psychosocial adjustment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the psychosocial and quality of life issues of women with breast cancer.
the psychosocial and quality of life issues that are faced by women who are diagnosed with early-stage breast cancer and who have completed their initial treatment and are in the process of recovery.
the psychosocial and health-related quality of life (HRQL) of women with early stage breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of tamoxifen is a safe and effective method to prevent breast cancer.
the quality of life of women with early-stage breast cancer is generally good, but that there are many factors that influence the level of well-being.
the evidence for the efficacy of chemotherapy in older patients with early breast cancer is limited and inconclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of social media is not only a way to reach the public, but also an effective tool in the hands of researchers.
the quality of life and the psychosocial adjustment of women aged 70 years or older who were diagnosed with breast cancer were similar to those of women who were 60 years old or younger.

we found that the older women who participated in our study had a very high quality of life in the 15 months after diagnosis, and they were generally well adapted to the psychosocial aspects of their breast cancer experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of women with advanced breast cancer have a positive quality of life.
we need to be more mindful of the impact of breast cancer on the quality of life for older women.
the majority of women in the study were able to maintain a good quality of life after their breast cancer diagnosis, but that a small number of women were not.
